title: Applause

translations.english: I stand here waiting for you to bang the gong
translations.chinese: 我站在這裡，等待你敲響那面銅鑼

translations.english: To crash the critic saying, "Is it right or is it wrong?"
translations.chinese: 以震耳的聲響擊碎評論家那句：「這究竟是對，還是錯？」

description: 《Applause》描寫一位表演者對舞台、掌聲與觀眾認同的強烈渴望。歌中的主角將觀眾的歡呼視為創作與表演的重要動力，渴望透過藝術展現自我，並從熱烈的掌聲中感受到存在的價值。面對外界的批評與質疑，她依然堅持自己的藝術理念，勇敢突破傳統與流行文化之間的界線。歌曲以閃耀的舞台、歡呼聲與藝術意象，呈現名聲帶來的興奮，以及對認可的深刻依賴。最終，《Applause》傳達的是藝術熱情、自我表達與追求肯定的複雜心情：掌聲能帶來鼓勵與力量，也可能令人逐漸依賴外界的評價，在創作自由與渴望被愛之間不斷尋找平衡。

vocabulary.usage: 要描述用力敲打銅鑼，讓它發出很大的聲音時，可以說 bang the gong。
vocabulary.prompt: 哪一句正確使用了「bang the gong」？
options: I bang the gong into my tea because it needs more sugar.
Please bang the gong quietly so nobody can hear it.
My ticket banged the gong and became a famous singer.
At the start of the show, a man will bang the gong.
optionExplanations: bang the gong 是敲銅鑼，不是把銅鑼加進茶裡；想讓茶更甜，可以說 I put more sugar in my tea.
bang 在這裡強調用力敲出響亮的聲音，與要求完全不被聽見的情境矛盾；可說 Please do not bang the gong.
票券不能自己敲銅鑼，更不會因此成為歌手；可說 My ticket lets me see the show.
表演開始時有人敲響銅鑼，動作與情境都正確。
vocabulary.explanation: 表演開始時有人敲響銅鑼，動作與情境都正確。

vocabulary.usage: 指經常評價電影、音樂、藝術或表演的人時，可以用 critic。
options: The music critic wrote about the singer's new song.
The critic opened at nine, but the door was still asleep.
I put two critics in the oven to make the cake taste better.
The critic is a new kind of chair, so please sit on it.
optionExplanations: 音樂評論家撰寫對新歌的評論，符合單字用法。
句子把評論家當作會開門營業的場所，還把門描述成睡著；可說 The shop opened at nine.
critic 是評論者，不是烘焙材料；可說 I put two eggs in the cake.
critic 指人，不是一種椅子；可說 Please sit on the chair.
vocabulary.explanation: 音樂評論家撰寫對新歌的評論，符合單字用法。

vocabulary.usage: 說一個人因作品或表現而受到許多人認識時，可以使用 fame。它是名詞。
options: I fame to the library after lunch.
The actor found fame after his first big movie.
The museum sells fame in small bottles for five dollars.
Her fame was late because it missed the train.
optionExplanations: fame 是名詞，不能當成「去」的動詞；可說 I go to the library after lunch.
演員在電影上映後獲得知名度，find fame 搭配自然。
名聲不是能裝瓶販售的商品；可說 The museum sells drinks in small bottles.
名聲不會自己搭火車，因此也不會因錯過火車而遲到；可說 She was late because she missed the train.
vocabulary.explanation: 演員在電影上映後獲得知名度，find fame 搭配自然。

vocabulary.meaning: 忍受、承受（此處為動詞）；另外也可指「熊」（名詞）。
vocabulary.usage: 想表達某件令人難受的事很難承受時，可以說 bear + 事情 或 can't bear + 事情。
vocabulary.prompt: 哪一句正確使用了「bear」作為「忍受」？
options: I can't bear this loud noise. Please close the door.
The bear at the zoo is eating fish.
The new building bears three blue windows.
I bear my name on the table before dinner.
optionExplanations: 噪音令人無法忍受，所以用 can't bear 很自然。
這句的 bear 是「熊」，句子本身沒錯，但沒有使用題目指定的「忍受」意思。
這句不是 A2 常見的 bear＝「忍受」用法；想表達窗戶數量，可說 The new building has three blue windows.
bear 不能在這裡代替寫名字的動作；可說 I write my name on the paper.
vocabulary.explanation: 噪音令人無法忍受，所以用 can't bear 很自然。

vocabulary.meaning: 為……而活；非常熱愛、重視某件事。
vocabulary.usage: 想強調一個人非常喜愛某項活動，或把它視為生活的重要動力時，可以說 live for + 名詞／活動。
vocabulary.prompt: 哪一句正確使用了「live for」？
options: The clock lives for seven o'clock and refuses to show eight.
She lives for music and plays the piano every day.
I live for this box because it has my old books inside.
Our hotel lives for six floors, but one floor is on holiday.
optionExplanations: 時鐘不會因為偏愛七點而拒絕顯示八點；可說 The clock shows eight o'clock.
每天彈琴的人非常熱愛音樂，lives for music 表達強烈喜好。
這裡只是說盒子裝著舊書，沒有自然表達「人生的重要動力」；可說 I keep my old books in this box.
樓層數量應用 has，不是 lives for；可說 Our hotel has six floors.
vocabulary.explanation: 每天彈琴的人非常熱愛音樂，lives for music 表達強烈喜好。

vocabulary.usage: 觀眾為表演者或隊伍發出歡呼聲時，可以用 cheer。
options: I cheered my name on the wall with a blue pen.
The sign says, “No cheering,” so the crowd cheered in silence.
The fans cheer when their team scores a goal.
Please cheer the painting into the kitchen; it is hungry.
optionExplanations: 寫名字用 write，不是 cheer；可說 I wrote my name on the wall with a blue pen.
句子把需要出聲的歡呼與完全無聲混在一起；可說 The crowd stayed quiet.
球迷在隊伍進球時歡呼，完全符合用法。
cheer 表示歡呼，不是搬動畫作的動作；可說 Please carry the painting into the kitchen.
vocabulary.explanation: 球迷在隊伍進球時歡呼，完全符合用法。

vocabulary.usage: 要關閉室內燈光時，可以說 turn the lights out 或 turn off the lights。
vocabulary.prompt: 哪一句正確使用了「turn the lights out」？
options: I turn the lights out of my bag and put them on a plate.
The workers turn the lights out when the show ends.
She turned the lights out by painting the ceiling green.
The street turns the lights out because it wants to sleep early.
optionExplanations: 這個片語不是從袋子裡把燈「倒出來」；可說 I take a lamp out of my bag.
表演結束後工作人員熄燈，正確描述關燈動作。
把天花板漆成綠色不等於關掉燈；可說 She painted the ceiling green.
街道不是會自己決定早睡的人；可說 The street lights turn off at midnight.
vocabulary.explanation: 表演結束後工作人員熄燈，正確描述關燈動作。

vocabulary.meaning: 無意間聽見、偶然聽到別人說話。
vocabulary.usage: 沒有刻意偷聽，卻剛好聽到附近的談話時，可以用 overhear。過去式是 overheard。
options: I overheard the soup and learned that it needed more salt.
The newspaper overheard a photo and became very worried.
I will overhear the meeting by putting it on the calendar.
I overheard two people talking about the concert on the train.
optionExplanations: 湯不會說話，無法讓人無意間聽見它的談話；可說 I tasted the soup and added more salt.
報紙不會聽見照片，overhear 通常與聽見人說話有關；可說 I saw a photo in the newspaper.
把會議加入行事曆是安排，不代表碰巧聽見談話；可說 I will put the meeting on my calendar.
在火車上無意間聽見別人談論演唱會，使用自然且符合語境。

vocabulary.meaning: 懷舊、對過去時光的想念。
vocabulary.usage: 看見舊照片、聽見以前的歌曲，而開始懷念過去時，可以使用 nostalgia。這個字是名詞。
options: Hearing that old song filled her with nostalgia.
My camera is full of nostalgia, so I need a bigger memory card.
The ticket office is closed because nostalgia has gone home.
The chef added three cups of nostalgia to the soup.
optionExplanations: 一首老歌勾起對過去的懷念，filled her with nostalgia 表達自然。
nostalgia 是懷舊感，不是佔用相機容量的數位檔案；可說 My camera is full of photos.
懷舊是感受，不是售票處的員工；可說 The ticket office is closed because the worker has gone home.
懷舊感不是可用量杯加入湯裡的食材；可說 The chef added three cups of water to the soup.
vocabulary.explanation: 一首老歌勾起對過去的懷念，filled her with nostalgia 表達自然。

vocabulary.usage: 事情沒有預警就發生，或情況很快改變時，可以用 suddenly。
options: We waited suddenly for six years, one minute at a time.
The guide says suddenly is the name of the oldest painting.
The music suddenly stopped, and everyone looked at the stage.
I bought three suddenly at the market for dinner.
optionExplanations: suddenly 不適合形容持續六年的漫長等待；可說 We waited for six years.
suddenly 一般用來描述動作發生得突然，不是畫作的種類；可說 The guide showed us the oldest painting.
音樂突然停止，大家因此看向舞台，符合副詞的用法。
suddenly 是副詞，不是市場裡可以買三個的物品；可說 I bought three oranges at the market.
vocabulary.explanation: 音樂突然停止，大家因此看向舞台，符合副詞的用法。
